hints: Focus on the words bilayer and cell surface membrane. Which type of molecule is famous for having a hydrophilic head and hydrophobic tails that line up in two layers?

Remember the fluid mosaic model applies to bacterial membranes too. Think about which option is the main structural lipid, and which options belong to the cell wall or are just parts of a larger molecule.
walkthrough:
**Recall what the cell surface membrane is made of**

All cells, including bacterial cells, need a partially permeable barrier around the cytoplasm. That barrier is the cell surface membrane, and its basic structure is the same in bacteria, plants and animals.

Key idea: membrane = phospholipid bilayer with proteins.

**Remember why phospholipids form a bilayer**

A phospholipid is amphipathic. It has a hydrophilic phosphate head that loves water and two hydrophobic fatty acid tails that avoid water. In water they automatically arrange tail-to-tail in two layers, with heads facing out.

**Apply this to a bacterial cell**

A bacterial cell still uses this phospholipid bilayer as its cell surface membrane. Peptidoglycan is outside the membrane in the cell wall, and bacteria do not use cholesterol in the way animal cells do. So the bilayer molecule must be phospholipid.

options.A: Fatty acids are only the tails of a phospholipid or triglyceride. They do not form a bilayer on their own.
options.B: Peptidoglycan forms the rigid bacterial cell wall outside the membrane, not the membrane bilayer itself.
options.C: Correct. Phospholipids with hydrophilic heads and hydrophobic tails form the bilayer of the bacterial cell surface membrane.
options.D: Cholesterol regulates fluidity in animal cell membranes and is not the bilayer molecule, and most bacteria lack cholesterol.
